A thermoelectric conversion module includes a thermoelectric conversion module body comprising a plurality of thermoelectric conversion module substrates. In each substrate, at least one of the following is provided on one surface of a flexible insulating substrate: a P-type thermoelectric conversion element including a P-type thermoelectric conversion layer and a pair of connection electrodes electrically connected to the P-type thermoelectric conversion layer; or an N-type thermoelectric conversion element including an N-type thermoelectric conversion layer and a pair of connection electrodes electrically connected to the N-type thermoelectric conversion layer. The plurality of thermoelectric conversion module substrates are arranged such that the direction of the connection electrodes and the direction of the insulating substrates are aligned.

The thermoelectric conversion module further includes a heat transfer portion provided on a side of the thermoelectric conversion module body adjacent to at least one connection electrode of the thermoelectric conversion module substrate. The heat transfer portion presses the thermoelectric conversion module substrate in an arrangement direction and transfers heat to the thermoelectric conversion module body or dissipates heat from the thermoelectric conversion module body. The heat transfer portion has a thermal conductivity of 10 W/mK or higher. When the thermoelectric conversion module substrate is pressed in the arrangement direction by the heat transfer portion, a normal stress in a direction perpendicular to a surface of the insulating substrate is 0.01 MPa or higher.

The thermoelectric conversion module includes a module body constructed from a plurality of thermoelectric conversion module substrates.

Each thermoelectric conversion module substrate includes a flexible insulating substrate. On one surface of the flexible insulating substrate, at least one thermoelectric conversion element is formed. The thermoelectric conversion element may be either a P-type thermoelectric conversion element or an N-type thermoelectric conversion element.

The plurality of thermoelectric conversion module substrates are arranged such that the direction in which the connection electrodes extend is aligned with the arrangement direction of the substrates. In addition, the direction of the insulating substrates is also aligned across the module body. This configuration allows the substrates to be stacked or arranged in a uniform orientation, thereby improving electrical connection reliability and thermal transfer efficiency.

A heat transfer portion is provided in the vicinity of at least one of the connection electrodes. The heat transfer portion is configured to transfer heat to the thermoelectric conversion module substrates or to dissipate heat from them. In addition, the heat transfer portion presses the thermoelectric conversion module substrates in the arrangement direction, thereby maintaining close contact between the relevant components and improving thermal conduction.

The heat transfer portion is made of a material having a thermal conductivity of at least 10 W/mK. Furthermore, the heat transfer portion applies a normal stress of at least 0.01 MPa in a direction perpendicular to the surface of the flexible insulating substrate. As a result, sufficient mechanical pressure and thermal conductivity are provided to enhance heat exchange performance and stabilize the operation of the thermoelectric conversion module.
outputs.L4:
A flexible thermoelectric conversion module includes a plurality of substrates arranged in a stacked, folded, or otherwise mutually facing configuration. Each substrate is provided with one or more thermoelectric elements, including P-type thermoelectric elements, N-type thermoelectric elements, or a combination of both. Connection electrodes are formed on the substrates so that, when the substrates are placed in the intended arrangement, corresponding electrodes are aligned with one another and electrically connect the thermoelectric elements in a desired circuit configuration, such as in series, in parallel, or in a combined series-parallel arrangement.

The module further includes a heat transfer portion positioned to contact or press the substrates together. The heat transfer portion may be formed from a thermally conductive material, such as a metal, ceramic, graphite-based material, thermally conductive resin, elastomer, or composite material. This portion serves both a mechanical and thermal function. Mechanically, it applies pressure in a direction substantially normal to the substrate surfaces, helping to maintain close contact between the substrates, thermoelectric elements, electrodes, and thermal interfaces. Thermally, it promotes efficient heat transfer between the module and an external heat source or heat sink, thereby increasing the temperature difference across the thermoelectric elements or improving heat dissipation during operation.

The heat transfer portion has a thermal conductivity of at least 10 W/mK. By providing this level of thermal conductivity, the heat transfer portion reduces thermal resistance and allows heat to be efficiently introduced into, removed from, or distributed through the thermoelectric conversion module. In addition, the heat transfer portion applies a normal stress of at least 0.01 MPa to the substrates. This pressure improves thermal contact, suppresses air gaps, and stabilizes electrical and thermal connections between the aligned components.

As a result, the flexible thermoelectric conversion module can maintain good thermal coupling even when used on a curved, irregular, or moving surface. The module can conform to various installation environments while preserving efficient thermoelectric performance. The combination of aligned connection electrodes, P-type and/or N-type thermoelectric elements, and a thermally conductive pressure-applying heat transfer portion enables improved heat transfer, enhanced heat dissipation, and stable power generation or temperature-control operation.
outputs.L5:
MPa stands for **megapascal**, a unit of pressure and stress commonly used in engineering, construction, materials science, and hydraulics. One MPa is equal to **one million pascals (1,000,000 Pa)**. Since the pascal is a relatively small unit, MPa is often more practical when describing high pressures or the strength of materials.

In construction and mechanical engineering, MPa is frequently used to express the **compressive strength of concrete**, the **tensile strength of steel**, or the pressure rating of pipes and hydraulic systems. For example, a concrete grade of **30 MPa** means the concrete can withstand a compressive stress of 30 megapascals before failure under standard test conditions.

MPa is also useful for comparing material performance. Stronger materials generally have higher MPa values, indicating they can resist greater forces without breaking, deforming, or failing. Because of this, MPa is an important measurement in product design, safety testing, and structural analysis.

In simple terms, **MPa helps engineers understand how much pressure or stress a material or system can handle**. It is a key unit for ensuring that buildings, machines, tools, and infrastructure are safe, reliable, and suitable for their intended use.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract describing a flexible thermoelectric conversion module with P-type/N-type elements, connection electrodes, aligned substrates, and a heat transfer portion with specified thermal conductivity and normal stress.
counterfactuals.output:
Abstract:  
A flexible thermoelectric conversion module includes a plurality of P-type thermoelectric conversion elements and N-type thermoelectric conversion elements alternately arranged in a predetermined direction, a plurality of connection electrodes electrically connecting the P-type and N-type thermoelectric conversion elements in series, and first and second flexible substrates disposed so as to face each other with the thermoelectric conversion elements interposed therebetween. The first and second substrates are aligned such that corresponding electrode-forming regions overlap in a thickness direction of the module. A heat transfer portion is provided on at least one surface of the module and is thermally coupled to the thermoelectric conversion elements through the connection electrodes and/or the substrate. The heat transfer portion has a thermal conductivity of not less than 0.5 W/m·K and is configured to exhibit a normal stress of not more than 1 MPa when compressed in the thickness direction, thereby maintaining heat-transfer performance while permitting bending or deformation of the module. The module can conform to a curved or movable heat source and efficiently convert a temperature difference into electrical energy or provide thermoelectric temperature control.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a technical description of an invention involving thermoelectric conversion module substrates arranged in alignment, where a heat transfer portion has thermal conductivity of at least 10 W/mK and applies at least 0.01 MPa normal stress.
counterfactuals.output:
A thermoelectric conversion device includes a plurality of thermoelectric conversion module substrates arranged in alignment along at least one direction. Each thermoelectric conversion module substrate includes a substrate body, a plurality of thermoelectric conversion elements electrically connected to one another, and electrode portions provided on or in the substrate body for electrically connecting the thermoelectric conversion elements. The plurality of thermoelectric conversion module substrates are positioned so that respective heat-receiving surfaces or heat-radiating surfaces thereof form a substantially continuous thermal interface.

A heat transfer portion is disposed in thermal contact with the aligned thermoelectric conversion module substrates. The heat transfer portion is configured to transfer heat between the thermoelectric conversion module substrates and an external heat source or heat sink. The heat transfer portion may be formed of a metal, ceramic, graphite-based material, composite material, or other thermally conductive material having a thermal conductivity of at least 10 W/mK. In some embodiments, the heat transfer portion has a thermal conductivity of 20 W/mK or greater, 50 W/mK or greater, or 100 W/mK or greater, thereby reducing thermal resistance between the thermoelectric conversion module substrates and the external thermal body.

The heat transfer portion is arranged to apply a compressive load to the thermoelectric conversion module substrates in a direction normal to a principal surface of each thermoelectric conversion module substrate. The compressive load produces a normal stress of at least 0.01 MPa at an interface between the heat transfer portion and the thermoelectric conversion module substrates. By applying the normal stress, interfacial gaps caused by surface roughness, warpage, or assembly tolerances are reduced, and thermal contact resistance at the interface is suppressed. As a result, heat can be efficiently conducted into or out of each thermoelectric conversion module substrate while maintaining mechanical positioning of the substrates in the aligned arrangement.

In one embodiment, the heat transfer portion includes a plate-shaped member extending across two or more adjacent thermoelectric conversion module substrates. The plate-shaped member may contact the aligned substrates directly or through a thermal interface material, such as thermal grease, a thermally conductive elastomer, a graphite sheet, a phase-change material, a solder layer, or a compliant metal layer. The heat transfer portion may be urged toward the thermoelectric conversion module substrates by fastening members, springs, clamps, an elastic frame, a housing, or a resilient heat-transfer member. The urging mechanism is selected such that the stress applied normal to the substrate surfaces is at least 0.01 MPa during operation, including during thermal expansion and contraction.

In another embodiment, the heat transfer portion includes a plurality of thermally conductive contact portions respectively corresponding to the thermoelectric conversion module substrates. The contact portions may be mechanically coupled to a common support or heat spreader. The common support maintains alignment of the thermoelectric conversion module substrates and distributes the compressive force so that each substrate receives sufficient normal stress for stable thermal contact.

The aligned arrangement of the thermoelectric conversion module substrates allows a thermoelectric conversion area to be enlarged while maintaining manufacturability and reliability of individual module substrates. The high thermal conductivity of the heat transfer portion promotes uniform temperature distribution among the plurality of substrates, thereby reducing temperature variation between adjacent modules. The applied normal stress improves thermal coupling and reduces the likelihood of localized thermal resistance, which can otherwise decrease thermoelectric conversion efficiency or cause thermal stress concentration.

The thermoelectric conversion device may be used either for power generation, in which a temperature difference between opposite sides of the thermoelectric conversion elements generates electrical energy, or for temperature control, in which electrical current supplied to the thermoelectric conversion elements produces heating or cooling by the Peltier effect. The device may be incorporated into waste-heat recovery systems, industrial heat exchangers, vehicle exhaust systems, electronic cooling assemblies, battery temperature control systems, or other equipment requiring efficient heat transfer through thermoelectric conversion modules.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3
